title: Noise-Adaptive Pager and Runbook Hints for Latency/Error SLOs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Objective: Reduce noisy, low-actionability P1 pages while preserving rapid detection of real SLO violations. Implement a noise-adaptive pager that stratifies signal by service and request-cardinality, augments alerts with ranked root-cause hints derived from recent trace clusters, and surface automated runbook suggestions in the Console page payload. Scope includes: tracer hook enrichment, metric/log pipeline enrichment, anomaly scoring model, alert rule changes (burn-rate tuning per-stratum), and dashboard/workflow additions for oncall and SRE.
background: We continue to get repeated pages where a single noisy downstream dependency or transient high-cardinality request pattern trips burn-rate windows. Current burn-rate rules are global per-service and generate many low-value wakeups. Recent incidents (see incident-2025-01-18) show that grouping by request shape and tag (tenant_id, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket) would have reduced noise and pointed oncall to the true contributing factor faster.
proposal_summary: 1) Add a lightweight cardinality sampler in the tracing hooks to record request_shape tags and latency buckets (low overhead, opt-in per service). 2) Enrich metrics and logs in ingestion with 'stratum' label computed from trace tags using the metrics pipeline (Kafka-hop transform). 3) Build a stratified anomaly scorer (statistical + simple ML) that computes burn-rate contribution per stratum and emits composite burn-rate alerts only when both global and top-n stratum scores exceed thresholds. 4) Include in alert payload: top 3 correlated trace clusters, likely root-cause tags, suggested runbook steps and suggested mitigation (scale, rollback, route fallback). 5) Add Console dashboard panel to inspect stratified burn-rate and runbook execution history.
non_goals: This ticket will not change the underlying billing or autoscaler policies. It does not implement a full ML retraining pipeline for anomaly models — model will be rules + lightweight classifier with manual tuning. It also does not change RBAC for who can acknowledge alerts.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: tracing hook overhead could increase latency. Mitigation: sample at 1% by default, add a strict CPU/memory budget, and run benchmarks in staging. Risk: label cardinality explosion in metrics store. Mitigation: hash-and-bucket request_shape into 64 buckets, and enforce retention/rollup in metrics aggregator. Risk: oncall confusion for enriched payloads. Mitigation: include brief human-readable summary and one-click link to actionable runbook in the page.
acceptance_criteria: New tracing hook deployed to staging for 3 services with <1% median latency regression
Metrics pipeline emits 'stratum' label and cardinality is capped to 64 buckets per service
Stratified burn-rate alerts fire in canary environment and reduce total page volume by >=30% in simulated noisy scenarios
Alert payload contains top-3 trace cluster links, two suggested runbook steps, and a Console link to stratified dashboard
Documentation and runbook templates added to Confluence and linked from the alert payload
implementation_notes:
- Tracing hooks: extend fast-trace-instrumentation v2 to emit request_shape fingerprint and sequence_length_bucket. See experimental branch: github.com/redwood-inference/tracing/compare/feat/strata-sample.
- Metrics pipeline: add Kafka transform in observability-ingest that computes 'stratum' = service + fingerprint_bucket. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability-ingest/pull/481.
- Anomaly scorer: initial implementation as a moving-window z-score with exponential smoothing; run as stateless microservice (obs-anom) with config in s3://obs-config/stratified-rules.yaml.
- Alerting: modify the burn-rate composer to accept per-stratum contributions and emit composite alert. Modify PagerDuty payload transformer to include extra fields and runbook links.
- Dashboards: add a Grafana dashboard 'Stratified SLO Explorer' and a Console panel that embeds it. Dashboard UID: obs_strata_202503.
- Feature flag: obs.stratified_paging (default off for prod), enable-by-prefix for canary services.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement tracing hook and metrics transform behind feature flag; deploy to staging for 3 non-critical services (auth, embeddings-preview, prompt-render). 2) Run 2-week simulated noisy workload using traffic-replay tool to validate false-positive reduction. 3) Enable stratified scoring in canary with alert suppression for existing global burn-rate rules for 48h. 4) If canary passes, gradually enable for more services in waves with SRE oversight. 5) Full prod enable after 6 weeks and retro with oncall.
monitoring_and_metrics: We will track: pages/week (baseline), median time-to-ack, number of alerts suppressed by stratification, top-strata contributor distributions, tracer overhead (p50/p95 latency delta), metrics-cardinality (unique strata/day), and false-positive rate in canary tests. Dashboards and SLOs for the feature itself will be added.
